shortDescription: India’s automobile industry faces a sharp moderation in production growth in early 2027, with light-vehicle output expected to grow 5.8 per cent against 18.8 per cent in the September quarter, two-wheeler growth slowing from 16.7 per cent to 5–7 per cent, and tractor production potentially contract…

children: India’s automobile industry faces a sharp moderation in production growth in early 2027, with light-vehicle output expected to grow 5.8 per cent against 18.8 per cent in the September quarter, two-wheeler growth slowing from 16.7 per cent to 5–7 per cent, and tractor production potentially contracting by 3–7 per cent. The changing outlook comes as CIE Automotive India, a Tier-1 and Tier-2 supplier to major automobile manufacturers, reported an 18.2 per cent increase in domestic sales but shrinking margins, highlighting the challenge component makers could face as vehicle production growth slows while raw-material and energy costs remain elevated.

The forecasts, drawn from industry estimates cited in CIE Automotive India’s October 22 investor presentation, suggest that the strong production momentum across passenger vehicles, two-wheelers and tractors during 2026 may become increasingly uneven in 2027.

The Pune-headquartered company, part of Spain’s CIE Automotive group, supplies forgings, castings, gears, stampings and engineered components across passenger vehicles, two-wheelers, commercial vehicles and tractors. Its reported customers include Mahindra & Mahindra, Maruti Suzuki, Tata Motors, Caterpillar and John Deere.
Growth slows as cost pressures persist
CIE’s Indian sales increased from ₹1,523.2 crore to ₹1,801 crore, an increase of 18.2 per cent, during July–September 2026, supported by strong automobile production.
However, EBITDA increased from ₹264.2 crore to ₹294 crore, an increase of 11.3 per cent, while its operating margin declined from 17.3 per cent to 16.3 per cent.
The company attributed the deterioration to higher raw-material, energy and consumable costs arising from the conflict in West Asia.
The pressure is particularly relevant because vehicle production growth is expected to slow across several categories.
Indian light-vehicle production increased from 1.52 million to 1.80 million units during the September quarter, while two-wheeler output rose from 6.93 million to 8.09 million units.

However, industry forecasts cited by CIE project light-vehicle growth moderating to 5.8 per cent in January–March 2027, two-wheelers to 5–7 per cent and tractor production declining between 3 per cent and 7 per cent.
The outlook for medium and heavy commercial vehicles has also been revised lower than earlier expectations, although the presentation does not specify a revised growth rate.
Europe offers a contrasting picture
While India’s automobile industry faces slower growth, Europe’s vehicle market remains weak, forcing component manufacturers to rely increasingly on cost reductions to protect profitability.
CIE’s European sales declined from ₹786.6 crore to ₹757.5 crore, a decrease of 3.7 per cent, during the September quarter.
Yet EBITDA increased from ₹110.6 crore to ₹123.8 crore, an increase of 11.9 per cent, while margins improved from 14.1 per cent to 16.3 per cent, reflecting restructuring undertaken during 2025.
European light-vehicle production is forecast to decline 2.2 per cent in the December quarter and 3.9 per cent in the first quarter of 2027
.Supplier earnings face a new test

CIE’s consolidated revenue from operations increased from ₹2,371.84 crore to ₹2,633.18 crore, an increase of 11 per cent, while profit after tax rose from ₹213.94 crore to ₹243.69 crore, an increase of 13.9 per cent.

The company is pursuing the merger of its wholly owned aluminium casting subsidiary into the listed Indian entity, subject to regulatory approvals. Its latest presentation does not quantify fresh capital expenditure, capacity expansion or revenue guidance.

For India’s component manufacturers, the next test may be less about meeting rapidly expanding production schedules and more about protecting profitability as growth moderates. CIE’s results show that margin pressure has already emerged before the anticipated slowdown in vehicle production.

title: India’s auto production boom set to slow in 2027 as CIE Automotive flags margin pressures
